free_tier.stated: No published volume cap; raw sequence data is redirected to SRA. Notable for retention rather than size.

tooling: GEO FTP/HTTPS plus the GEOmetadb / GEOquery R packages.
chaining: Not a volume play. The interesting property is private-retention: records may stay private for up to four years before release, with reviewer tokens for anonymous read-only access.

limits.value: approval step (~5 business days for accession)

limits_note: per-object-cap: not stated (defer to SRA for raw reads). Retention: 'the maximum allowable limit is four years' for private hold, then mandatory public release; records can be edited after release. Binding constraint is the human curation/approval step (~5 business days for accession).
reliability_note: Records cannot stay private once an accession is cited in a manuscript or preprint — GEO staff release unilaterally.

evidence.proved: 'the maximum allowable limit is four years', forced release if accession cited
5 business days for accession, private-until-published policy

notes: No published volume cap; raw sequence data is redirected to SRA. Notable for retention rather than size.
binding_note: the write is a queue with a person or a rule in it, so the upload rate is set by somebody else
